source.title: Predicting the Generalization Ability of a Few-Shot Classifier
source.authors: Myriam Bontonou; Louis Béthune; Vincent Gripon

record.file_problem: The supplied text is a full paper. Its first-page title, “Predicting the Accuracy of a Few-Shot Classifier,” differs from the metadata title, but the text is internally coherent.
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies few-shot task accuracy and metrics for predicting it. It does not test the listed versions about random-label memorization, width, convolutional versus fully connected networks, optimizer or batch-size comparisons, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or removing memorized examples.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results on few-shot classifier test accuracy and predictors of that accuracy. These findings concern a related few-shot setting not covered by the listed versions. It also cites prior work and reports figure-only results; cited findings are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures variability and predicts accuracy in transfer-based few-shot classification. None of its experiments tests V1–V8. Its feature-space overlap, confidence and clustering measures do not measure magnitude-aware weight sharpness or train–test gaps (V7). Using Adam and convolutional backbones without the relevant comparisons does not test V3 or V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly matches the authors' conclusion: they attribute task difficulty mainly to relationships between base and novel classes, find setting-specific measures correlated with performance, and report useful accuracy prediction from LR confidence without additional labeled validation samples. The base-class explanation is an interpretation of the overlap analyses, rather than a controlled causal result.
record.recipe_differences: Transfer-based few-shot evaluation using pretrained feature extractors and few-shot classifiers; not a study of the listed interventions or standard training comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: Task difficulty and predictor correlations vary with class selection, shot count, number of ways, query count, and class balance. The text also reports that class choice generally produces more accuracy variability than shot choice in its mini-ImageNet experiment.

fits_no_version.finding: Accuracy ranged from 55.6% to 98% across 10,000 tasks; varying classes produced greater accuracy variability than varying shots in the main experiment.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Transfer-based few-shot accuracy varies substantially across tasks, with class selection contributing more variability than shot selection in this setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Summed class-overlap scores correlated 0.84 with LR error; overlap-graph edge weights correlated 0.93 across two backbones.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Feature-space class overlap tracks few-shot classification error and is similar across the two tested backbones.

fits_no_version.finding: The confidence-based accuracy predictor had reported error of 2.40 percentage points versus 4.14 for the constant predictor.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Classifier confidence can predict task accuracy in the tested semi-supervised few-shot setting.

fits_no_version.finding: DB-score had absolute correlations of 0.64 and 0.72 with N-means ARI at 20 queries per class.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Cluster separation tracks clustering quality on the tested few-shot feature representations.

record.problems: The few-shot results use transfer-based features and do not assess the listed standard-training versions. Several plotted correlations and comparisons are not numerically recoverable from the supplied text. Task accuracy and its predictors are evaluated on the paper's specified sampled tasks and datasets.
record.rows_left_out: Figure-only values for correlation curves and the sample-selection comparison were not transcribed as numeric rows because the supplied text gives no exact values. Results cited from other work were excluded.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization under the same architecture and recipe.
Width sweeps beyond zero training error and their effects on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization, local connectivity and transferred initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD generalization under limited or broader tuning and recovery interventions.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout effects, underfitting, small-data conditions and removal with weight decay.
Magnitude-aware weight sharpness, train–test gaps and comparative ranking against norm and margin measures.
Removing highly memorized training examples versus removing random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8, not judgments that the reported few-shot findings are absent. The supplied text identifies itself as arXiv:2007.04238v1, Predicting the Accuracy of a Few-Shot Classifier; its correspondence to the supplied DOI remains unresolved. Section VI-D also swaps sensitivity and false-positive-rate values in its semi-supervised prose relative to Figure 9's confusion matrix.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out accuracy on natural labels under the same training recipes.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation and their effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons and local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization comparisons and tuning or recovery conditions.
Large versus small batch comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout and weight-decay interventions on held-out error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of train-test gaps against other measures.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.

rows.subject: wideresnet with LR
rows.size_stated: Wide Residual Network, 28 layers and width factor 10; classifier size not stated
rows.stage_stated: feature extractor trained on mini-ImageNet; LR trained for few-shot task
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated test accuracy across 10,000 random 5-way 5-shot tasks
rows.locator: Section IV, Case Study on mini-ImageNet
rows.note: The paper reports the range across a sample of 10,000 runs.
rows.check: The accuracy range is correctly transcribed, but it cannot establish any listed version.

rows.subject: wideresnet with LR
rows.size_stated: Wide Residual Network, 28 layers and width factor 10; classifier size not stated
rows.stage_stated: feature extractor trained on mini-ImageNet; LR trained for few-shot task
rows.operation_detail: Measured variability in task accuracy over random tasks, fixed-class tasks with random shots, and fixed-shot tasks with random classes
rows.value: 5.85% over random tasks; average 2.02% with fixed classes and random shots (standard deviation 0.35%); average 4.37% with random classes and fixed shots (standard deviation 0.61%)
rows.uncertainty: Standard deviations stated for the averages: 0.35% and 0.61%
rows.locator: Section IV-A, Identifying the source of overfitting
rows.note: The authors report greater variability from changing classes than from changing shots in this experiment.
rows.check: The numbers are correct but measure task-accuracy variability, not any listed effect. Class and shot selection are not independent; Section IV-A explicitly qualifies this interpretation.

rows.subject: densenet-m with LR
rows.stage_stated: feature extractor trained on mini-ImageNet; LR trained for few-shot task
rows.operation_detail: Compared summed class-overlap scores for sampled five-class tasks with LR generalization error
rows.measure: Pearson correlation between summed overlap score and generalization error
rows.note: The test set used the 595 remaining examples.
rows.check: The 0.84 correlation is correct. This is feature-space class overlap versus classification error, not weight sharpness versus train–test gap.

rows.subject: densenet-m and wideresnet
rows.operation_detail: Compared class-pair overlap scores across backbones
rows.locator: Section IV-B3, Influence of the backbone; Figure 1 caption
rows.note: The paper says the graphs are very similar.
rows.check: The 0.93 correlation is correct but compares overlap graphs from two convolutional backbones. It supplies no convolutional-versus-fully-connected generalization comparison.

rows.subject: wideresnet with LR
rows.size_stated: Wide Residual Network, 28 layers and width factor 10; classifier size not stated
rows.stage_stated: feature extractor trained on mini-ImageNet; LR trained for few-shot task
rows.operation_detail: Compared LR confidence predictions of task accuracy with a constant-accuracy baseline
rows.measure: Mean absolute error of predicted accuracy
rows.baseline: Naive method always predicting the same accuracy: mean absolute deviation 4.14%
rows.note: The text says the LR-confidence predictions are better than the naive method.
rows.check: This is the study's proposed accuracy predictor compared with a constant predictor, so it should be excluded from claim-evidence rows. The reported errors are 2.40 versus 4.14 percentage points. Section VI-D's interpretation of confidence as predicted accuracy is also inconsistent with the negative-log confidence definition in Equation 19.

rows.subject: wideresnet with LR
rows.size_stated: Wide Residual Network, 28 layers and width factor 10; classifier size not stated
rows.stage_stated: feature extractor trained on mini-ImageNet; LR trained for few-shot task
rows.operation_detail: Measured correlation of Davies-Bouldin score with N-means adjusted Rand index as query count varied
rows.measure: Linear correlation between DB score and ARI
rows.note: The authors state that 20 samples per class are sufficient to increase the correlation up to 0.64.
rows.check: The subject should be N-means clustering on diffused wideresnet features, not wideresnet with LR; no LR is trained in this unsupervised experiment. The reported 0.64 is an absolute Pearson correlation, not a signed positive correlation.

rows.subject: densenet-t with LR
rows.stage_stated: feature extractor trained on tiered-ImageNet; LR trained for few-shot task
rows.operation_detail: Measured correlation of Davies-Bouldin score with N-means adjusted Rand index as query count varied
rows.measure: Linear correlation between DB score and ARI
rows.note: The authors state that 20 samples per class are sufficient to increase the correlation up to 0.72.
rows.check: The subject should be N-means clustering on diffused densenet-t features, not densenet-t with LR. The reported 0.72 is an absolute Pearson correlation, not a signed positive correlation.
